research_question: How do group count and learned features per group trade off parameter efficiency, FashionMNIST accuracy and reference-to-Q.ANT numerical agreement in hierarchical g4 QFourier architectures?
observations: Exp023's 16-group, 4-feature hierarchy outperformed monolithic g4 while using fewer parameters.
Only one hierarchical topology has been tested, so it is unknown whether 16x4 is near a useful frontier.
hypothesis: A local search over hierarchical low-fan-in topologies will reveal multiple non-dominated designs, and reducing first-stage fan-in will generally improve Q.ANT numerical agreement while feature width controls representational capacity.
falsification_criterion: The hypothesis is weakened if alternative hierarchical topologies show no systematic relation between first-stage fan-in and numerical agreement, or if none provides a meaningful accuracy/parameter trade-off relative to the Exp023 16x4 design.
limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
This is a bounded local architecture search, not an exhaustive optimization.
Different group counts require contiguous equal-size partitions of the 784 flattened pixels.
